title: Alto o alta? Gli aggettivi e l'accordo
summary: Adjective agreement (four endings vs two), where adjectives go, and the shortened bello/buono

blocks.title: Adjectives agree
blocks.body: Adjectives must **agree** with the noun they describe, in gender and number. Adjectives ending in **-o** have four shapes: *alto/alta/alti/alte* (tall). Adjectives ending in **-e** only have two shapes — the same for masculine and feminine: *intelligente* (sing., either gender), *intelligenti* (pl., either gender).
blocks.callout: Four shapes or two — the adjective always has to match its noun.

blocks.title: Before or after? bello & buono
blocks.body: Most adjectives **follow** the noun (*una casa grande*). But a handful of everyday ones — **bello**, **buono**, **grande** — usually go **before**, and they shorten a little there, almost like *un/il* do: *un buon caffè* (a good coffee), *una buona idea* (a good idea), *un bel libro* (a nice book), *una bella giornata* (a nice day).
blocks.callout: After essere they stay full-length: 'il caffè è buono', not shortened — the shrinking only happens right before the noun.

pairs.note: -o adjectives flex for gender and number; -e adjectives only flex for number.

blocks.prompt: Which is correct: 'the girls are intelligent'?
blocks.explain: intelligente only changes for number, not gender: plural is intelligenti either way.

blocks.prompt: Which is correct for 'a good coffee'?
blocks.explain: buono shortens to buon before a masculine singular noun starting with a consonant: un buon caffè.

blocks.prompt: Type 'a nice house' in Italian — bello goes before the noun here.
blocks.hint: casa is feminine — bello agrees and sits before it.
blocks.explain: *Una bella casa* — bella agrees with the feminine casa and comes before it.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the whole line.

blocks.scene: Marco tells you about Giulia's cozy apartment near Via Mazzini

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: L'appartamento di Giulia è bello, ma piccolo.
lines.en: Giulia's apartment is nice, but small.
lines.spotlight: bello here follows essere, so it keeps its full form — shortening only happens right before the noun.

lines.speaker: You
lines.en: Small? How many rooms does it have?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Due stanze, ma luminose. E lei è una persona molto ordinata.
lines.en: Two rooms, but bright. And she's a very tidy person.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Giulia sembra una donna intelligente e simpatica.
lines.en: Giulia seems like an intelligent and nice woman.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Esatto! E il suo caffè è sempre buono.
lines.en: Exactly! And her coffee is always good.

blocks.prompt: Describe two people you know using at least three different adjectives — check that the endings agree!
